about: Swiss Grid house look (fixed; one house look per style, new components every reel). Ported from LemoLab's MIT-licensed Swiss Motion Graphics style (lemo-opuscar styles/swiss-motion: STYLE.md, DEMO.md, demo/ease.js + film.js), adapted to a 9:16 talking head. CREDITS.txt.
world: International Typographic Style in motion around a talking head: the 9:16 frame is a modular page; the speaker's face, as shot, lives in one horizontal band of it between a paper header (caption row + counter) and a paper page (their words set flush left on the grid); between face worlds the page grows up over the frame into short full-screen poster cards (giant numeral chapter cards, a grid being built, a grid that means something); one signal colour = the reel's one protagonist, the only thing allowed to be inexact

frame.note: 6 columns of 130 px, 24 px gutters, 72 px left margin, content ends at x 972 (Instagram's action column keeps ~100 px of the right edge). The header is a 300 px paper strip; the page starts 40 px under the bottom of the speaker's head box in the window (face_track grown box), so the face, as shot, is never covered. Text stays between y 120 and 1700.

palette.note: page, paper, ink, greys and ONE signal colour. The signal colour is the reel's one protagonist (in the proof reel, a phone): the opening line under the header, its slab, the minutes it takes, the module that leaves the grid. Nothing else is red; real pictures go grey (a red-pink book cover is shown in greyscale). Overprint allowed: black type on the signal colour. No gradients, shadows, grain, glow or blur.

type.family: Inter (OFL, rsms), variable 100-900, Latin + Cyrillic woff2 from templates/fonts. One family for the whole reel (the source used Archivo, which has no Cyrillic).

numeral.note: figure height ~700 px (cap 0.7275 em), optically flush left: x - lsb (house numeral_lsb_em)

type.rules: flush left, ragged right, every line on a column start; lowercase allowed in headlines; the speaker's words exactly as said (a fix only for a wrong transcription, e.g. a misspelt name); every string checked for glyph coverage at build time; nothing under 48 px.

motion.ease: cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1) for every snap (JS function SW in the page); linear for lines being drawn and for the exception. No overshoot, no spring, no bounce, no fades, no blur.

note_values.note: 30 fps: a sixteenth = 4 frames, an eighth = 8 frames; onsets rounded to whole frames

motion.entrances: words rise out of a clip rect from below the baseline in a sixteenth, starting on their spoken onset; they leave upward in an eighth; paper (cards, pages) appears by a wipe of its edge; lines grow along their length (linear); giant numerals climb in 4 eased steps
motion.deletions: knife cut: a 3 px ink line crosses the element in a sixteenth (linear), then the element collapses to its midline in an eighth
motion.ripples: ordered by distance from their cause, two units per sixteenth
motion.exception: the signal element only: linear, unsnapped, one eighth pause mid-flight, a readout beside it turns from 'on grid' to 'off grid'

sound.rule: the voice + SFX only, NO music bed. Foley of print, dry: a sound only where something enters or is cut (paper wipe = paper-flip, block snap = wood-hit, type / row clack = click-1, knife = shutter-1, ruling pen = pencil-write trimmed, slide = wood-plane, the exception leaving = whoosh-1 soft); none on single caption words.
sound.never: a music bed, a sting, a meme sound, an unlicensed (licensed: false) file

budgets.pictures: drawn graphics first (type, bars, modules, grids); a real picture only for a thing the speaker names (e.g. a book cover), greyscale, placed on the grid like an artifact with a museum label

film: the speaker's face as shot: no grade, no filter, no crop, no scale; the header and page cover only what is above the head and the chest below the chin
vary_per_reel: what the grid means (e.g. 60 cells = the 60 minutes of an hour)
the chapter programme (how many numbered chapters and which lines open them)
the poster cards and their compositions
the exception's move and the ending
the knife-cut lists, bars and modules
grade_rule: none: the speaker's footage stays as shot; the only real picture (a named thing) goes greyscale for the one-signal-colour rule
components_rule: one house look (grid, type, palette, motion, header + page, caption row, print foley); the poster cards, protagonist shape, list devices, the grid that means something, the exception's move and the ending are NEW every reel (catalog.json)
